## 1. Identity summary

He has over nine years of professional work on web products, public APIs, integrations and developer tooling, mostly in TypeScript, JavaScript, React and Node.js, with Python in production (Oneflow CRM integrations) and Rust in shipped open-source and desktop work. He holds an MSc in Computer Science from Uppsala University and an MSc in Operations Research and Computer Applications from NIT Tiruchirappalli, and two peer-reviewed papers on energy-efficient data communication for the mobile Internet of Things.

From April 2017 to December 2024 he worked at Oneflow AB in Stockholm, a digital signature and contract management platform, as JavaScript Developer, Full Stack Integration Engineer (built and led the Integration Team), Engineering Team Lead, then Senior Software Engineer.

Since December 2024 his role has been Independent AI/SI product and systems engineering (agentic workflows). In that time he shipped:

- adaptate, a TypeScript validation library on npm (adaptate, @adaptate/core, @adaptate/utils).
- kanithanj, a local-first decision app (Tauri, Rust, React, SQLite); 1.0.0 on 19 August 2026 and 1.3.0 on 23 November 2026. Source: https://github.com/p10ns11y/collab-finder.
- Ensembly, a Rust operator kernel for one shared SQLite ledger and one approval flow.
- Agent plugins and a skills library for Grok Build, Cursor and Claude Code.
- A Next.js portfolio and CV pipeline from one data source.

Most of his deep-learning and systems work is private. The public repositories are a record that grew slowly.

## 5. Shipped work, in technical depth

### 5.1 adaptate: typed, validated data from any schema or stream

Links: https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate · https://adaptate-site.vercel.app · npm: adaptate, @adaptate/core, @adaptate/utils

adaptate is a TypeScript library built from scratch. From 25 October to 23 November 2026, npm downloads were @adaptate/core 1,092, @adaptate/utils 987 and adaptate 864 (counts include CI and bots), or about 1,000 a month per package. 2.4.2 of all three packages was published on 24 November 2026 from CI with SLSA provenance (https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1). First commit 2 November 2024 (f506830); first npm publish on 4 November 2024.

The problem. One data model is used by many screens, each needing different fields, so copies of the schema drift. A model also streams a tool call as JSON, and `JSON.parse` throws until the last byte arrives, so the UI shows nothing.

Design.

- One schema, many views. `transformSchema(schema, config)` in @adaptate/core takes one Zod schema and a consumer field config, and returns a Zod schema with the same inferred type.
- OpenAPI interop both ways in @adaptate/utils, including `$ref` resolution.
- Streaming validation of LLM tool-call JSON as it arrives (`createAgUiPartialValidator`, `createStreamValidator`, `parseStream`), including a Result API so an AI/SI model's tool call can be checked at the boundary.

Numbers. On a 966-character sample, the incremental feed made 966 character visits; re-parsing the growing buffer made 68,304. Tests run converters on documents 100,000 levels deep. A `$ref` chain past depth 500 throws `RangeError`. CI fails a pull request if a timed case is more than 5% slower than its base, and packed tarballs are checked on TypeScript 7 and 6.

### 5.2 kanithanj: a local-first decision app (Tauri, Rust, React, SQLite)

Site: https://kanithanj-ai.vercel.app · source: https://github.com/p10ns11y/collab-finder · walkthrough: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/shipped/collab-finder

Releases v1.0.0 (19 August 2026) to v1.3.0 (23 November 2026). A Rust backend with a SQLite ledger, LLM routing across providers, the xAI API, and secrets in the OS keyring. The model is called only when cost, fit and rate checks pass. A person approves before anything leaves the machine. Personal data never leaves disk. CI runs `cargo test` and Stryker mutation testing. Kanithanj began as a private desktop app he uses daily and is now heading to public use once fully actualized. XState runs the settings panel in the app; model-based tests walk it, not only in tests.

### 5.3 Ensembly: one shared ledger and one approval flow

Link: https://github.com/thecuriousts/ensembly · essays: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/articles

A Rust operator kernel that gives several coding-agent tools one shared SQLite ledger and one approval flow. Bots and harnesses propose; Ensembly authorises, claims and completes. One writer owns the ledger, with idempotent retries.

### 5.4 Agent plugins marketplace

Link: https://github.com/p10ns11y/plugins (first commit 15 July 2026). One repository of plugins that install into Grok Build, Claude Code and Cursor, bundling skills, commands, agents and hooks, including pulse-memory, live-engine, and routing and planning plugins.

### 5.5 Agent skills library

Link: https://github.com/p10ns11y/skills (first commit 8 June 2026). A library of `SKILL.md` procedures for context, coordination, supply-chain hardening, reviewable PRs and related work. In the README's words: "Most agent failures are not model failures. They are context, coordination, and guardrail failures."

### 5.6 devprofile: portfolio, CV pipeline and agent profile

Links: https://captain.kingsparrow.space · https://github.com/p10ns11y/devprofile (first commit 8 September 2025). Next.js 16, React 19 and TypeScript. One `cvdata.json` file drives the site, the PDF CV and the agent profile files, so content cannot drift. The site serves `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` as plain text.

### 5.7 imm: independent module maintainer

Link: https://github.com/p10ns11y/imm (first commit 22 September 2026, Rust). A supply-chain tool that installs a direct dependency as source and keeps other uses as hashed, audited extracts. An agent cannot approve its own extract.

### 5.8 proposales-planner-bench

Links: https://proposales-planner-bench.vercel.app · https://github.com/p10ns11y/proposales-planner-bench (first commit 6 October 2026). A public Next.js bench against the Proposales API, used to validate API readers with adaptate and to try planner-style workflows. Named after that API; it is a benchmark, not a product for that company.

### 5.9 thepulimaangani: Tamil prosody in the browser

Links: https://github.com/p10ns11y/thepulimaangani · walkthrough: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/shipped/thepulimaangani. A Rust parser for Tamil metre, compiled to WebAssembly, with a React UI. The analysis runs in the browser with no backend.

## 6. Build lifecycle and focus

Map: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/building (published 31 August 2026, redrawn as a life-cycle loop on 22 October 2026).

He works from one priority list. Most of his 183 public GitHub repositories are forks or coursework; /building names 16 active projects in five clusters. Work goes into one portal, Grok Bot with Ensembly as its memory and decision model. Retired or melted projects return as raw material.

- April 2020 → April 2026: thepulimaangani returned as a Rust/WASM parser.
- 2 November 2024: adaptate started; 2.4.2 shipped on 24 November 2026.
- 11 April → 30 May 2026: premflow, a C CLI, was rewritten on elomaxz, his C MVU framework, a day after elomaxz started (commit f1804b3).
- 6 July 2026: he grouped 13 recently started projects into clusters for agents (X, 6 July 2026).
- 12 July 2026: Ensembly replaced a dormant 2016 app with a new control layer (commit 4f35ce1). Tag v0.1.0, annotated that evening, marks the last pre-rewrite commit.
- 19 August 2026: kanithanj (repository collab-finder) started as a private desktop tool for his job search and shipped 1.0.0 as a public app.
- 3 September 2026: botify fused the plugins and skills repositories into shareable Grok Bot templates.
- 7 September 2026: packedbox melted arch-machine and shellyxz.sh into one portable Linux bootstrap. Both sources were kept.

kanithanj depends on @adaptate/core. Skills began as procedures lifted from devprofile and premflow (8 June 2026). Ensembly and participatory-mesh (8 September 2026) share one model: authorise and claim, then dispatch.

As of 25 November 2026 these projects have not yet served other people: 0–3 GitHub stars, no outside issues or code, and adaptate's roughly 1,000 monthly npm downloads include CI and bots, so outside use is unknown. Posts drew 5 to 144 views on X. Next: open kanithanj once it works for his own search.

## 7. How I work

- Measure before trusting: retrieval benchmarks before ranking changes; performance budgets that fail a PR more than 5% slower.
- Rules enforced by tooling: README examples run as tests; hooks that ask before `git push` and deny force-push.
- Verify before irreversible acts: merges, releases, payments, deletions.
- Small, reviewable PRs; one source of truth for data.
- The same idea since his MSc research (IEEE CloudCom 2015): cut the cost of each observation while decisions improve. Today that means agents load only the context that can change the next step. Essays: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/articles
- Dated notes and earlier working methods: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/ideas.md
